pr.title: Also InstSimplify `&raw*`
pr.description:
We do this for `&*` and `&mut*` already; might as well do it for raw pointers too.

r? mir-opt
pr.author: scottmcm

processing.reason: The PR is a pure missed-optimization extension: it teaches InstSimplify to rewrite `Rvalue::AddressOf(_, place)` when `place` ends in `Deref` and the rvalue type exactly matches the dereferenced base type, turning `&raw const (*p)`/`&raw mut (*p)` into `p`. The before/after MIR diffs show only identity assignments such as `_6 = &raw const (*_1) -> _6 = _1` and `_8 = &raw mut (*_2) -> _8 = _2`; the type-mismatched cases remain untouched. Thus the historical (pre-extension) and new (post-extension) behaviors are semantically identical on every input, including the test's six reference/pointer cases. There is no value-changing wrong transformation to encode, and any claimed original/transformed difference would have to be manufactured by adding unrelated return-value changes, which the task forbids. Therefore no source-grounded counterexample pair can be validated.

analysis.summary: Extends InstSimplify's reference-of-deref simplification from `Rvalue::Ref` to also cover `Rvalue::AddressOf`, but only when the rewritten rvalue's type exactly equals the dereferenced base place's type. The regression test deliberately includes six reference/pointer cases so that only the type-matching subset simplifies.
analysis.originalLogic: `InstSimplifyContext::simplify_ref_deref` only matched reference rvalues: `if let Rvalue::Ref(_, _, place) = rvalue {`, then looked for `if let Some((base, ProjectionElem::Deref)) = place.as_ref().last_projection() {` and returned early if `rvalue.ty(self.local_decls, self.tcx) != base.ty(self.local_decls, self.tcx).ty`. Thus it implemented the documented rule `// Transform `&(*a)` ==> `a`.`` for `&*` and `&mut*`, but not for raw-pointer address-of forms.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historical (pre-extension) behavior: `&raw const (*a)` and `&raw mut (*a)` were left untouched by InstSimplify even when the address-of expression was a pure identity on the dereferenced base; only `Rvalue::Ref` was rewritten. The PR extends the match to `if let Rvalue::Ref(_, _, place) | Rvalue::AddressOf(_, place) = rvalue {`, so `_6 = &raw const (*_1);` becomes `_6 = _1;` and `_8 = &raw mut (*_2);` becomes `_8 = _2;` in the pointers test. This is a missed optimization, not a value-changing wrong rewrite.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies containing either `Rvalue::Ref` or `Rvalue::AddressOf` whose operand place's last projection is `ProjectionElem::Deref`, with either reference bases (`&T`, `&mut T`) or raw-pointer bases (`*const T`, `*mut T`), and with a possible type mismatch between the produced pointer/reference and the dereferenced base.
analysis.trigger: An rvalue is `Rvalue::Ref(_, _, place)` or `Rvalue::AddressOf(_, place)`, the place ends in a `Deref` projection, so it has shape `&(*base)`, `&mut (*base)`, `&raw const (*base)`, or `&raw mut (*base)`.
preconditions: The last projection of the place must be `ProjectionElem::Deref`, yielding a `(base, ProjectionElem::Deref)` pair.
The result rvalue type must be exactly equal to the dereferenced base place type: `rvalue.ty(...) == base.ty(...).ty`; otherwise the pass must return without rewriting.
The original rvalue must be either `Rvalue::Ref` or `Rvalue::AddressOf`; other rvalue kinds are out of scope.
pitfalls: Do not assume every `&*x`, `&mut *x`, `&raw const *x`, or `&raw mut *x` simplifies: the test states `only 2 of the 6 should simplify, as the others have the wrong types.`

Reference and raw-pointer types are not interchangeable by this pass: e.g. `&raw const (*_2)` where `_2: *mut i32` produces `*const i32` but the base type is `*mut i32`, so it is intentionally not simplified.
Do not treat a retained test name or an old CHECK comment as proof of pass behavior; compare the actual MIR assignments in the before/after diff.

The early type-equality guard is a semantic/type-correctness invariant, not an optional optimization condition; dropping it would produce type-incorrect MIR when mutable/const or reference/pointer types differ.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a `tests/mir-opt/instsimplify/` test using `//@ test-mir-pass: InstSimplify`, `#![feature(raw_ref_op)]`, and inline `EMIT_MIR ...InstSimplify.diff` / `CHECK` annotations. Cover both `references(&i32, &mut [i32])` and `unsafe fn pointers(*const [i32], *mut i32)` with six cases each: `&*`, `&*` on mutable, `&mut *`, `&raw const *` on const, `&raw const *` on mut, and `&raw mut *`. Assert that only the type-matching cases simplify (e.g. `// CHECK: _3 = _1;` and `// CHECK: _4 = &(*_2);` in the references test; `_6 = _1;` and `_8 = _2;` in the pointers diff), leaving the mismatched forms unchanged.
evidence: +        if let Rvalue::Ref(_, _, place) | Rvalue::AddressOf(_, place) = rvalue {
// For each of these, only 2 of the 6 should simplify,
// as the others have the wrong types.
We do this for `&*` and `&mut*` already; might as well do it for raw pointers too.
